firmwares.name: zp12
firmwares.author: zvenson
firmwares.what: A 12-bit sampler after the E-mu SP-1200: sample on the FM-1 itself (a computer or phone plays into it over USB) or in the browser (mic, line-in or a file), and it plays on its own. Gritty and unsmoothed, with loops and songs.

data.what: A 12-bit sampler after the E-mu SP-1200: sample on the FM-1 itself (a computer or phone plays into it over USB) or in the browser (mic, line-in or a file), and it plays on its own. Gritty and unsmoothed, with loops and songs.

firmwares.name: Hortator
firmwares.author: DEADACTIVE
firmwares.what: A drum machine: eight tracks of drums, a step sequencer, Grids, a pumping compressor, LFOs, resonators and live effects. Play it in the browser first.

firmwares.name: Felucca
firmwares.author: Leo Kuroshita (Hügelton Instruments)
firmwares.what: The custom firmware the others build on: the FM-1's own synth engines, a sequencer, effects and a better panel, with an editor in the browser.

firmwares.name: Felucca [Salt]
firmwares.author: Chance Roth (ChanceTheMaker)
firmwares.what: Felucca with a hardware-inspired Studio in the browser (play it there without an FM-1): many engines, presets, skins. A beta.

firmwares.name: Jangada
firmwares.author: zednaked
firmwares.what: Dark, industrial, Brazilian: drones that breathe, ten engines (6-op FM, a superwave analog with a ladder filter), four tracks, a mod matrix, live effects.

firmwares.name: GHOULBOX
firmwares.author: Jason Persinger
firmwares.what: Dungeon synth: a cathedral hall reverb, tape and crush, a hurdy-gurdy engine, choirs, organs and recorded psaltery and harp, an old-RPG screen with wall torches.

firmwares.name: Melodee
firmwares.author: keremimo
firmwares.what: Total playing pleasure, far beyond Felucca: recording without quantize, microtonal scales, a Casio CZ-1, a bit-by-bit Dexed, scale modes made for an MPC Sample as its companion.

firmwares.name: SLOOP
firmwares.author: isod89
firmwares.what: A live groovebox: tracks, layers, a step sequencer, song mode, punch-in effects and samples, played on the FM-1 in real time.

firmwares.name: Clipper
firmwares.author: isod89
firmwares.what: A deep synth grown out of SLOOP: 23 engines and 407 sounds, from HYBRID (three oscillators, two filters, a mod matrix) to six-operator FM, wavetables, wave sequencing, a Juno and physical models; arp, step sequencer, MPE and a web editor for every parameter.

firmwares.name: Bubba Machine
firmwares.author: Erbubar23
firmwares.what: A six-track groovebox written from scratch: TR drums from Plaits' 808 and 909 models, a sampler with a 16-slice slicer, a bass and three free tracks (analog, 6-op FM, 303 acid), scenes and fills, all at 44.1 kHz.

firmwares.name: SLOOP Floyd FM
firmwares.author: René Bohne
firmwares.what: SLOOP with a visual four-operator FM engine after Floyd Steinberg's 4-OP idea: an ADSR per operator, seven pages, a live oscilloscope that draws the envelopes as you play.

firmwares.name: SLOOP DX7 Banks
firmwares.author: majnikool
firmwares.what: SLOOP 2.4 with up to twelve DX7 voice banks, kept and named in the editor, presets by kind. Test builds: back up first.

firmwares.name: sloopDX
firmwares.author: zvenson
firmwares.what: SLOOP's live workflow with Dexed's DX7 engine and 128 steps a track: six operators, 32 algorithms, your own .syx banks, every voice edited on the FM-1, FM drums you program.

firmwares.name: X0X
firmwares.author: Charles Vestal
firmwares.what: A groovebox: 909 and 808 drums, two 303s with TB-3PO, a breakbeat generator and song mode.

firmwares.name: X0X-RMX
firmwares.author: Mr-Roboto (Oliver)
firmwares.what: X0X remixed after The Orb: banks and patterns reordered live per voice, Grids MAP and EUCLID drum generation, an extended TB-3PO with 22 scales and a morphing 303 waveform. Built on X0X.

firmwares.name: FoMni
firmwares.author: Charles Vestal
firmwares.what: A chord harp inspired by the Omnichord: strum the white keys, pick chords on the black ones.

firmwares.name: ChoralRoot
firmwares.author: Quixotic7
firmwares.what: A Telepathic Orchid-style chord instrument: one hand plays roots, the other shapes chords; voicings, performance modes, bass and a looper.

firmwares.name: WaveLoop FM-1
firmwares.author: ELI7VH
firmwares.what: Felucca played from an Arturia MiniLab 3: track faders, a DJ filter, momentary effect pads; 32 patches a bank, 12 evolving songs, revoiced 808 and CR78 kits.

firmwares.name: OberVave
firmwares.author: zvenson
firmwares.what: An 8-voice analog-style poly in the spirit of the classic American polys of 1979-84, now on four tracks: each its own sound, arp and sequence; a mixer with chorus, delay, plate reverb and drive sends, a master with DJ filter and compressor. Tracks start on the bar, patterns keep their sounds.

data.what: An 8-voice analog-style poly in the spirit of the classic American polys of 1979-84, now on four tracks: each its own sound, arp and sequence; a mixer with chorus, delay, plate reverb and drive sends, a master with DJ filter and compressor. Tracks start on the bar, patterns keep their sounds.

firmwares.name: Shine On
firmwares.author: zvenson
firmwares.what: A string ensemble in the spirit of the late-70s machines, grown out of OberVave: divide-down keyers with 16', 8' and 4' footages, register filters, a BBD ensemble and a phaser per sound. Now on four tracks with a mixer, delay, reverb, drive, a master and the step sequencer.

data.what: A string ensemble in the spirit of the late-70s machines, grown out of OberVave: divide-down keyers with 16', 8' and 4' footages, register filters, a BBD ensemble and a phaser per sound. Now on four tracks with a mixer, delay, reverb, drive, a master and the step sequencer.

firmwares.name: Dinghy
firmwares.author: zvenson
firmwares.what: Your base for your own FM-1 or SMK-37 firmware: everything under it done and documented (updates, USB rescue, MIDI over USB and the TRS jack with clock, USB audio, keys, screen, flash storage, an update screen), a 4-voice sine on top, tests and a CI that releases with attestation. Fork it, replace the sine.

firmwares.name: FiMba-1
firmwares.author: jadamsowers
firmwares.what: A physically modelled kalimba: tines laid out like the real one, thumb-roll chords, mbira patterns, a sound hole to cover, grains, tape and a plate reverb. Play it in the browser first.

firmwares.name: JIANT FM
firmwares.author: juanjiant-bit
firmwares.what: A bio-synthetic groovebox: six tracks drawn as living beings in thermal colours, eight engines (FM6 with Dexed, analog, phase, voice…), mutating macros, song mode from SLOOP. Not yet tested much on a real FM-1.

firmwares.name: fm1-chord
firmwares.author: math0ne
firmwares.what: A chord machine after the HiChord, with extras: chords in a key under the white keys, slash chords and inversions, sounds, envelopes, effects and a looper.

firmwares.name: FuMi-1
firmwares.author: cartesive
firmwares.what: A shigin conductor after the Suiko ST-50: its two rows of keys, the key set in honsū, equal or its own just tuning, a koto and twelve more sounds on a 6-op FM engine, ring time, vibrato, trill and a looper.

firmwares.name: MAKU
firmwares.author: okumurari
firmwares.what: An ambience machine for DJ interludes: switch it on and a random world in key plays, four parts, buttons that are verbs, and the worlds you like breed new ones. Clock follow. Play it in the browser first.

firmwares.name: Rainbow Mode
firmwares.author: joshbartlettband-web
firmwares.what: A music toy for little children: 63 cartoon friends, every key in tune, chords, strumming, songs to follow and an ear game, notes on a staff, a volume cap for small ears.

firmwares.name: AMB-1
firmwares.author: Charles Vestal
firmwares.what: A generative ambient machine after Music for Airports: it plays itself from the start, breathing voices, bells on tape loops of unequal length, a gliding bass. You do not perform it, you tend it.

firmwares.name: CTL-1
firmwares.author: Charles Vestal
firmwares.what: A MIDI controller: notes in any scale with its chords on the black keys, four banks of knobs, an arpeggiator and Euclidean drums, with General MIDI sounds of its own when nothing is connected.

firmwares.name: winampFM Synth
firmwares.author: Hericdk
firmwares.what: Winamp 2.x on the FM-1, built on SLOOP: your sounds as a playlist, four tracks you record as loops, effects on sliders and a visualizer made of lines. The real firmware plays in a 3D simulator first.

firmwares.name: MYCELIUM
firmwares.author: Mandalars
firmwares.what: Forest, Psytrance, Goa and Hitech grooves, built on Felucca and SLOOP: original drums and icons and four factory songs. A test release: not yet fully tested on the device.

firmwares.name: Polly
firmwares.author: Charles Vestal
firmwares.what: A pocket arranger after the QY70: pick a style, play three keys for a chord and a band of eight follows, songs from sections, General MIDI sounds from Sonivox EAS, and a General MIDI module over MIDI in.

firmwares.name: ETCH
firmwares.author: SikkenWorks
firmwares.what: Draw the sound: a waveform drawn and changed with the knobs, saved, morphed into another one, and a third waveform modulating the result.

firmwares.name: FM-106
firmwares.author: PatttF
firmwares.what: The Juno-106 emulation of KR-106 ported to the FM-1: six voices on both cores, the BBD stereo chorus, 128 factory presets and a 1980s Roland look.

firmwares.name: TRIBE
firmwares.author: apiel
firmwares.what: A ten-track groovebox where any engine plays on any track: kicks, 909 and 808 voices, the 303, sixteen clips a track, scatter effects and four master knobs you assign. Built on X0X.

firmwares.name: DUELL
firmwares.author: OSCILL/R
firmwares.what: A multimorphing bitimbral synthesizer: two complete parts, three ways to play them together, and a morph that glides between two versions of every sound.

data.what: A MULTIMORPHING bitimbral synth: two complete parts, three ways to play them together, and a morph that glides between two versions of every sound. Ten engines including wavetables, twin filters, effects and a mod matrix. Layer, dual or stereo mode. Velocity sensitivity and aftertouch. Dual core.

firmwares.name: Skiff
firmwares.author: illuminus5
firmwares.what: Six tracks of synths and drums with a groovebox's workflow: fourteen engines, a 64-step sequencer with chords, ratchets, trig conditions and locks, songs, PERFORM with scenes, six themes and a browser editor; FM6 sounds built from scratch on the unit. Built on Felucca, with most of Felucca 1.6.1's work brought over (the second core, MIDI LEARN, INSERT); Felucca's sounds and projects load. Also runs on the SMK-37 Pro.

firmwares.name: Fart Machine One
firmwares.author: adamcharleswilsonmusic-code
firmwares.what: A questionable musical instrument: ten artisanal farts, reverb, delay and a sixteen-step sequencer.

firmwares.name: ORBIT
firmwares.author: dspaudio
firmwares.what: A four-track groovebox: three synths and a drum machine in a colour-coded Synth, Drum, Event Tape and Mixer workflow, loops turned into songs, user macros, screens after the OP-1. Based on SLOOP.

firmwares.name: Felucca 8 Patterns
firmwares.author: echoe
firmwares.what: Felucca 1.5.1 with eight sequences a track to switch between and chain one after another; the user samples are left out to make room.

firmwares.name: PIGEON
firmwares.author: The Shrimp Blimp
firmwares.what: An old-school hip-hop and house sampler after the SP-404 and the PO-33: two song samples and a 16-pad kit, up to 32 chops a song, a 64-step sequencer, patterns and a song arrangement. Built on Felucca.

firmwares.name: CS-1
firmwares.author: twochannels
firmwares.what: A Yamaha CS-80 in spirit: eight voices of two channels, high- and low-pass filters in series, ring modulator, the touch response and 22 tones from the owner's manual. A sound module played over MIDI.

firmwares.name: HYP-1
firmwares.author: RedtailWorks
firmwares.what: Hypnotic techno and acid: a breathing pad, a deep drone, a generative 303 line and grain over drums you sequence. Flip patterns on the bar, break it down, build it up. Forked from AMB-1. One of a pack of four: LOF-1 (a lofi groovebox), ECO-1 (a plant plays it) and GRAV-1 (a star and its planets), experimental, on its project page.

firmwares.name: Tonitor
firmwares.author: Nuno Zimas
firmwares.what: Six tracks for live ambient and experimental music: three synth engines, patches generated by algorithm, free-length loops with up to ten overdubs each, a granulator, filters and a lush reverb.

firmwares.name: NOIZ DEMONS
firmwares.author: SPIKE the Percussionist
firmwares.what: Felucca with randomization as a ritual: every new sound summons one of 30 demons of the Ars Goetia, its sigil takes the screen and its rank decides how wild the sound gets.

firmwares.name: CoralFlower
firmwares.author: FicusFicusov
firmwares.what: Chords after the Orchid, with controls made for the FM-1: one key plays a chord with a bass note. Also 27 scales, an arpeggiator, a sequencer with drums and a song mode, and a pixel flower that grows as you play.

firmwares.name: Vector37
firmwares.author: genkigenki
firmwares.what: An orbiting overtone synth: four corners of two overtone generators each, a sun on a path and a moon around it decide how much of each you hear; the knobs shape the selected planet. Made for the SMK-37, here its FM-1 build. After the Beetlecrab Vector.

firmwares.name: MC-1
firmwares.author: dspaudio
firmwares.what: An original four-part groovebox with a 1990s workflow: three melodic parts and a 16-lane drum part, 128 melodic presets, eight drum kits, song arrangement, an arpeggiator and recorded knob moves.

firmwares.name: BEETLE
firmwares.author: Joppe Sikken (SikkenWorks)
firmwares.what: A tracker for the FM-1: patterns written top to bottom, step by step, with note, instrument, chord and effect columns, the way trackers have always worked.

firmwares.name: MIN-1
firmwares.author: Reytian
firmwares.what: A tiny minimalist ensemble after Philip Glass: it starts playing when you switch on, you join whenever you like. In EASY mode every white key is a chord that fits. Four models, twenty pieces.

firmwares.name: PurpleMonkey
firmwares.author: Quixotic7
firmwares.what: A first instrument for toddlers: random key bashing and knob turning are rewarded with dancing animated pets and little musical sequences. Press a key, any key.

firmwares.name: Pocket GammaWave
firmwares.author: ShadowTune (GammaWave Audio)
firmwares.what: The companion to the GammaWave desktop synth: four industrial distortions, vowel and scream filters, an FFT spectrogram, a four-track tape deck screen and a song generator with 49 genres, trap and drill too.

firmwares.name: Tuna
firmwares.author: delirioux
firmwares.what: Generative music built on Felucca: composer profiles write the music as it plays, you steer them. A work in progress.

firmwares.name: Frodhes
firmwares.author: Leonardo Mirabal
firmwares.what: An electric piano, vibraphone and marimba, physically modelled, no samples, with drive, tremolo or wah, phaser, chorus, delay and reverb (hall, plate, infinite), tap tempo and MIDI clock sync, an arpeggiator, a sequencer, scales and presets.

firmwares.name: FOMAJAM
firmwares.author: konsumer
firmwares.what: A drum machine in the classic step-grid style: voices after the 909, 808, 707, 606, DMX and more, a machine per voice, accents and patterns. Play it in the browser first.

firmwares.name: KAWA
firmwares.author: Omnipotard (Guizmoh)
firmwares.what: A pocket tracker for any style: six tracks with an engine each (pulse, 4-bit wave, noise, 6-operator FM, drum kit or sample), patterns chained into a song, 32 live effects and tools that write beats for you. A beta, not yet tried on a real FM-1 by its maker.

firmwares.name: No Man Sky FM
firmwares.author: Hericdk
firmwares.what: A space adventure while you make music, built on SLOOP 2.7.1: fly between planets with two knobs, land, mine, fight sentinels and warp between stars, every SLOOP screen floating over the game.

firmwares.name: FM1 Quest
firmwares.author: Hericdk
firmwares.what: A pixel-art RPG while you make music, built on SLOOP: four heroes, one a track, walk through a village and fight monsters and bosses as your loop plays, every SLOOP screen redrawn in the game's style.

firmwares.name: GR!MM
firmwares.author: GRiMMBIENT
firmwares.what: Dark ambient, dungeon synth and deathdream: four tracks, seven sound sources from VA and 6-op FM to formant voices and physical models, tape, granular freeze and reverbs up to infinite, a 64-step sequencer and song mode. Built on Dinghy.

firmwares.name: Cut-A-Dor
firmwares.author: Kid Bunka
firmwares.what: A beat dojo for scratch DJs and beatmakers: boom bap, lo-fi and breaks from 16 rhythm families with swing and fills, an eight-lane 32-step sequencer, punch-in effects you record bar by bar, a bass voice. Sound banks and editor in the browser.

firmwares.name: Mutable Dreams
firmwares.author: Kid Bunka
firmwares.what: A generative instrument after a small modular setup: six freely assignable tracks, 15 engines (selected Plaits, Rings and Elements algorithms and voices of its own), 288 tones and 92 Biomes, 32-step phrases with live recording, chord journeys, a granular cloud and named User Banks. Plays and edits live in the browser.

firmwares.name: FM1-GM
firmwares.author: jartificer
firmwares.what: A General MIDI sequencer with 16 tracks, 128 General MIDI instruments to choose from and a drum kit (on track 10). It can store up to 64 songs, each containing up to 128 measures.

firmwares.name: 386DX
firmwares.author: seajaysec
firmwares.what: A karaoke robot with a band: it sings songs from karaoke and MIDI files, or lines you type, to the notes you play. Its face is the voice. Keys, bass and drums play along, with a step sequencer and sixteen punch-in effects.

firmwares.name: Bunker Evolved
firmwares.author: Kid Bunka
firmwares.what: Generative ambient: four editable layers from 64 sound recipes, 24 worlds, 24 motifs and 32 scales. GROW varies the phrases, seven EVOLVE processes change them over time. Felucca's sound pages stay. Built on Felucca 1.6.1.

firmwares.name: OPN-1
firmwares.author: putchdev
firmwares.what: The Sega Genesis / Mega Drive's Yamaha YM2612: six channels of 4-operator FM. Its web app takes patches from game music (VGM) and OPM files and streams VGM tunes to the FM-1 to play.

firmwares.name: SID-1
firmwares.author: putchdev
firmwares.what: The Commodore 64's SID chip, twice for six voices. Its web app edits patches and takes them straight from .sid game music files.

firmwares.name: Mini-Tone
firmwares.author: Stéphane Schmitz
firmwares.what: Felucca with six tracks and new engines: SID, Braids' 48 models, a TB-303 and engines after Elektron's Analog Four, SY Chip and Digitone 2, a ping-pong delay and a new reverb. Built on Felucca 1.5.

firmwares.name: MORPHEUS
firmwares.author: Ben Badio
firmwares.what: A pattern sequencer after Reason's Matrix: up to four channels of MIDI sequence data out, and a few voices built in to build the patterns with.

firmwares.name: FMini-1
firmwares.author: Ruppert
firmwares.what: A three-oscillator monosynth in the spirit of the classic Moogs: a 24 dB/octave ladder filter, two contours, 100 factory patches, an arpeggiator, a sequencer and MIDI. Built on Felucca.

firmwares.name: DUB-1
firmwares.author: sbegueria
firmwares.what: A generative dub techno machine that plays itself from the moment it is on: chord stabs into a tape echo, FM pings, a sub bass on five grooves, a ducking kick, crackle, and an eight-bar arrangement with breaks and fills.

firmwares.name: Ketch
firmwares.author: risseraka
firmwares.what: A tracker in the LSDJ / picoTracker / M8 line: song, chain and phrase screens, instruments, effects and a mixer, on the FM-1's own keys and screen.

firmwares.name: FMEL-1
firmwares.author: Antonio Altea
firmwares.what: Mellotron-style tape sounds, coloured with effects and lo-fi tape: flutes, strings and choirs as on the old tape frames, played from the keys.

firmwares.name: ZEN-1
firmwares.author: aceyprime
firmwares.what: Ambient as a living window: cherry petals on a river, koi in a pond, fireflies under a real moon, and every movement a note. Set it down and let it play; the keys play along, the knobs shape the scene.

firmwares.name: Golana
firmwares.author: Gadlele
firmwares.what: One analog-style synth laid out like the classic microKORG, with a screen that draws the sound.

firmwares.name: Golana DZ Edition
firmwares.author: dzwerg
firmwares.what: Golana's synth with a sequencer for whole songs: 64 steps a pattern, 32 programs (up to 2,048 steps), a SONGMODE that plays from a first to a last program once or on repeat, and USB MIDI out to sequence other synths.

firmwares.name: MODELAR
firmwares.author: Hirakos
firmwares.what: A semi-modular drone synth played like a Kaoss Pad: four oscillators modulating each other through eight routings, and keys that move a cursor on an XY pad instead of playing notes: white keys are points, black keys gestures. ARP, a polymetric sequencer, a clock in Hz and eight generative environments.

firmwares.name: Niagara Drift
firmwares.author: evanyerburgh
firmwares.what: A drone synth: two drifting virtual-analog drones, each with its own part, swells, LFOs, effects and a sequencer.

firmwares.name: Unholy Union
firmwares.author: actuallysparky
firmwares.what: Generative ambient and drone: Immaculate Permutation rolls an arrangement in one key, a pad, a sequence and a chord arpeggio under a fourth voice for your hands. Keep a sermon you like, evolve it, or reveal another.

firmwares.name: Evander's Music Box
firmwares.author: Michail Tsakiroglou
firmwares.what: A bard's instrument for LARP, medieval and high fantasy: recorder, hurdy-gurdy, harp and a tavern kit on four tracks, encounters and songs for the table. "Mother Melody hears thy song."

firmwares.name: Chipbox
firmwares.author: Pasquale Barilla
firmwares.what: A chiptune groovebox with replicas of the NES, Game Boy and Sega Master System sound chips, in three views: RACK for the 16 steps of a page, CHIP to set up each channel, SONG to chain the pages into a song.

firmwares.name: LOOM-8
firmwares.author: Charles Vestal
firmwares.what: A groovebox inspired by the OP-XY: eight tracks on nine engines, step tricks and locks, weave, a conductor and throws.

firmwares.name: MONK-1
firmwares.author: Charles Vestal
firmwares.what: Twelve singers, from Jerry the monk to Snider the punk, each in its own voice: MonkSynth's formant voices, played with velocity and pressure from the FM-1's own keys.

firmwares.name: Flyfish
firmwares.author: delirioux
firmwares.what: One piece on the FM-1: Chopin's Étude Op. 10 No. 1 on a sampled Steinway D. It plays the étude, lets you shape it with rubato, touch and accents, practise it and move it. Built on Tuna and Felucca.

firmwares.name: Bytemania
firmwares.author: lloyd (llozd)
firmwares.what: A bytebeat synth: play one-line formulas, tweak them with the knobs, and write your own, with a random button in the formula creator that is really fun. A beta, built on Dinghy.

firmwares.name: HERA
firmwares.author: Ben Badio
firmwares.what: A chord groovebox after the Roland J-6: 100 chord sets, 9 phrase styles with 12 variations each and a 64-pattern step sequencer, on a four-voice Juno-style synth from Clipper with chorus, delay and reverb. A chord map on the screen shows which chord sits on which key. Built on Dinghy.

firmwares.name: FRASIL
firmwares.author: Styves Goupil
firmwares.what: An ambient drone and texture instrument: tap a key to latch a drone, a note or a chord in your key, press to swell it. Three layers a voice into a big reverb with shimmer and freeze; GLINT plays icy FM bells on top, by hand, by arpeggiator or a 32-step sequencer, and BASS holds a deep note below.

firmwares.name: Tessera
firmwares.author: Theo Dainis (Rastapopolix)
firmwares.what: Generative music on four tracks: each plays its own steps, an arpeggio or one of 13 generators (Turing, Euclid, Markov, Constellation, Chord and more), and the tracks evolve, follow and modulate each other. EVOLVE and FORM grow phrases into songs; 16 mod cords connect anything. A Melodee fork.

data.what: A generative four-track firmware: each track plays steps, an arpeggio or one of thirteen generators (Turing, Euclid, Markov, Atlas, Chord and more). Phrases evolve into song forms, tracks follow and answer each other, and 16 mod cords connect anything. FM, Trio and drum sounds.

firmwares.name: Del Rio
firmwares.author: Jess Del Rio
firmwares.what: A rhythm box of ceremony percussion: djembe, cajon, udu, clapsticks, maracas and triangle, their real strokes on the black keys, a step sequencer on the white keys and 31 rhythms from the literature. Played alone: a berimbau with its caxixi, a buzzing tanpura and a breathing shruti box. Built on fm1-base.

firmwares.name: Carnac OS
firmwares.author: OrbVorgis
firmwares.what: A dual-timbral wavetable synth after Carnac's standing stones: 15 morphing wavetable banks, seven voice architectures, a MAQ 16/3-style sequencer for modulated sequences and a chord sequencer for progressions, spring, tomb and tank reverbs. Its own installer also writes its wavetables. Built on X0X and Felucca.

firmwares.name: DRIFT
firmwares.author: FBNFRTG
firmwares.what: An ambient instrument for live sessions: warm synths, spacious pads and delicate plucks over a generative Euclidean sequencer on one track, with delays and reverbs from spring to shimmer. Built on Felucca.

firmwares.name: SIDOU
firmwares.author: Denis Sablić
firmwares.what: Turns the FM-1 into a C64 SID machine: two SIDs (6581 and 8580) with the chip's character dialled in, a GoatTracker 2 compatible tracker and step sequencer, and a live instrument to play over a song.

data.what: Turns the FM-1 into a C64 SID machine: two SIDs (6581 and 8580) with the chip's character dialled in, a GoatTracker 2 compatible tracker and step sequencer, and a live instrument to play over a song.

firmwares.name: MNM-1
firmwares.author: Veff
firmwares.what: Six monophonic tracks of synth and FX machines, pages of eight knobs, a filter and a tape delay on every track, three LFOs a track, parameter locks and slides. Forked from Hortator, with sounds ported from MONO2K.

firmwares.name: MONO2K
firmwares.author: Iñigo Hernandez
firmwares.what: Six mono machines in the spirit of Elektron's Monomachine: FM, superwaves, wavetables, a SID, a voice and four drum synths, one per track. A 64-step sequencer with parameter locks, trig conditions and ratchets, a lofi bus, four demo parts and a web patch editor.

data.what: Six mono machines in the spirit of Elektron's Monomachine: FM, superwaves, wavetables, a SID, a voice and four drum synths, one per track. A 64-step sequencer with parameter locks, trig conditions and ratchets, a lofi bus, four demo parts and a web patch editor.

firmwares.name: Caravel
firmwares.author: BonszaiMusic
firmwares.what: Felucca continued: a multi-engine synth with ANALOG, SEM, HADES, PHASE, TRIO, a tonewheel, FM6, physical models, voices, samples, grain and slices, drums, noise and an experimental DRONE engine. Pair Morph blends two engines, a HOME screen of your own and free macros a track for live sound design.

firmwares.name: MIDIMON
firmwares.author: ignis32
firmwares.what: A MIDI monitor for USB, the TRS jack and Bluetooth (as device and host at once): hex or words, filters, stats. Its THRU routes, each filtered, make the FM-1 a Bluetooth MIDI dongle.

data.what: A MIDI monitor for USB, the TRS jack and Bluetooth (as device and host at once): hex or words, filters, stats. Its THRU routes, each filtered, make the FM-1 a Bluetooth MIDI dongle.

firmwares.name: Makohai
firmwares.author: delirioux
firmwares.what: A generative groovebox in the style of early-90s PC tracker music: six lanes (lead, arp, pad, bass, drums, sfx) composed live in ten S3M-scene styles. You mix styles instead of programming steps. Built on Tuna and Felucca.

firmwares.name: ESTAMPIE
firmwares.author: Drew Robinson
firmwares.what: A groovebox for lively mediæval dance music: hurdy-gurdy, lutes, shawms and frame drums over drones, four tracks with 64-step sequencers, mediæval modes and temperaments, and velocity from the FM-1's own keys. Built on GHOULBOX and Felucca.

data.what: A groovebox for lively mediæval dance music: hurdy-gurdy, lutes, shawms and frame drums over drones, four tracks with 64-step sequencers, mediæval modes and temperaments, and velocity from the FM-1's own keys. Built on GHOULBOX and Felucca.

firmwares.name: FIZZ
firmwares.author: Quixotic7
firmwares.what: A groovebox around one engine, ChoralRoot's FM TONE: eight tracks, p-locks and preset sound locks, conditions, ratchets, chords, and MIDI FX for generative patterns and for reworking the ones you have.

firmwares.name: Matryoshka
firmwares.author: glvno
firmwares.what: A modular synth you patch in the browser: modules (oscillators, filters, envelopes, delays) nest into assemblies you save and reuse, and the patch plays on the FM-1, polyphonic with a Voicing module.

firmwares.name: Loom FM-1
firmwares.author: Co-oscillator
firmwares.what: Four synth and sampler tracks and a drum track on 14 engines, among them wavetable, 6-op FM, tape scrub, granular and a slicer; a 64-step sequencer, a chord progression generator, macros and sidechain ducking.

firmwares.name: TastyWaves
firmwares.author: marksweiss
firmwares.what: A 12-voice wavetable synth: two oscillators a voice, a resonant filter, two envelopes, an LFO, four effects, an arpeggiator and two step sequencers for chords and counterpoint; load your own Serum, WaveEdit, Ableton or Surge tables.

firmwares.name: Arctic Scream
firmwares.author: p0larpatch
firmwares.what: Dark ambient drones and feedback screams from the frozen tundra. Built on GR!MM, with HOWL, a feedback-loop voice after the Synthux Audrey II that wakes out of silence and grows into a howl, and 46 arctic sounds.

firmwares.name: S1Vave
firmwares.author: Andrew GG
firmwares.what: A synth after the Roland S-1 and the SH-101: a punchy sub-oscillator, a resonant filter, bass and lead sounds and hands-on controls for playing live. Built on OberVave.

firmwares.name: GATOR
firmwares.author: ivanvoid
firmwares.what: A monophonic macro-oscillator on the open Plaits DSP: all 24 models with harmonics, timbre and morph, an 8-slot mod matrix fed by an envelope, two LFOs, velocity, aftertouch and random, a low-pass gate, and a DRONE mode.

firmwares.name: Monohull
firmwares.author: Mark White
firmwares.what: A monosynth: one voice with analogue-modelled oscillators and five filters (ladder, diode ladder, OTA, Sallen-Key, state-variable), unison, chorus, delay and reverb, and 14 presets.

firmwares.name: PERF-1
firmwares.author: deamonSLINKY
firmwares.what: A generative groovebox you perform on: ten genres of self-playing pieces, an auto-DJ with breakdowns, builds and drops, Euclidean drums, an acid line that answers itself, beat FX and DX7-style FM voices from your own .syx.

firmwares.name: J6
firmwares.author: JackieAlacrity2373
firmwares.what: A six-voice JUNO-60 style polysynth with chorus, arpeggiator and a 16-step recorder.

data.what: A six-voice JUNO-60 style polysynth with chorus, arpeggiator and a 16-step recorder.

firmwares.name: GuitChordi
firmwares.author: Stoogs
firmwares.what: A chord and string instrument: 16 synthesized sounds, 50 chord styles, editable voicings, guitar tunings, and Freeplay, Strum and Arp modes with partial-chord pulses.

data.what: A chord and string instrument: 16 synthesized sounds, 50 chord styles, editable voicings, guitar tunings, and Freeplay, Strum and Arp modes with partial-chord pulses.

firmwares.name: Ravel
firmwares.author: De-Pattern
firmwares.what: An eight-track groovebox for sound design: thirteen synth engines, struck percussion and 33 drum machines after the Machinedrum, on an influence grid where any track can trigger, excite or modulate any other.

firmwares.name: Berlinan
firmwares.author: Jiří Píša
firmwares.what: A generative Berlin School MIDI sequencer: voices that repeat, phase on loops of unequal length and earn their mutations over time. The FM-1 makes no sound itself: each voice goes out over USB on its own MIDI channel to your synths.

fmhub.error: what: 20 to 300 characters of plain text, no HTML, no links

firmwares.name: MOPE-1
firmwares.author: slothpallas
firmwares.what: A sad wavetable synth played by a pixel blob in a rainy room: its eyes are the filter, its mouth the envelope, its tears the delay. Toy-keyboard accompaniment with 13 gloomy beats, auto-bass, arpeggiator, loop recorder.

firmwares.name: Kitten Synths
firmwares.author: Black Kitten Devices
firmwares.what: SLOOP with kittens: three synth tracks, a light synth and drums, 13 engines incl. MUUG (a Minimoog-style voice from FMini-1 with 100 sounds), 37 drum kits, your own samples, 27 punch-in effects, 64 steps and audio recording.

data.what: Groovebox con el motor MUUG (tipo Minimoog, 100 sonidos), una cuarta parte sintetizadora LITE y temática de gatos negros. Basado en SLOOP.

firmwares.name: Nauclerus
firmwares.author: Mr. Roboto
firmwares.what: Hortator's eight-track groovebox taken further: ORB Remix with 256 pattern mappings, the TB-3PO acid melody generator with 22 scales, more acid waveshaping, four bipolar LFOs and Grids rhythms copied into editable steps.

firmwares.name: PT/FM
firmwares.author: hitosu
firmwares.what: A ProTracker-style pocket studio: DX7 FM, JUNO-106, TB-303, chip, sampler and FUSION instruments side by side, 16 voices on both cores, a loop station, a two-deck DJ mode, punch-in effects and over 500 built-in instruments.
